events.title: Leo X condemns the errors of Luther
events.shortBlurb: The bull Exsurge Domine censured forty-one propositions of Martin Luther and gave him sixty days to recant…
body: By 1520 the writings of Martin Luther, an Augustinian friar of Wittenberg, had spread through Germany and won him the protection of princes. After a Roman commission examined his works, Leo X on 15 June 1520 issued the bull Exsurge Domine — 'Arise, O Lord' — condemning forty-one propositions drawn from them as heretical, scandalous, false, or offensive to pious ears.

The bull gave Luther sixty days to recant, and Johann Eck published it in Germany that autumn. Luther answered with defiant pamphlets, and on 10 December 1520, the day the grace period expired, he publicly burned the bull together with volumes of canon law at the Elster Gate of Wittenberg.

Leo X replied on 3 January 1521 with the bull Decet Romanum Pontificem, pronouncing his excommunication. Summoned that spring before the emperor Charles V at the Diet of Worms, Luther refused to retract, and the breach that became the Protestant Reformation stood open.
